description: BHAGWAN MAHAVIR WILDLIFE SANCTUARY Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, located in the Western Ghats of Goa, is the largest wildlife sanctuary in the state, covering an area of about 240 square kilometers. It is home to diverse flora and fauna, including Bengal tigers, leopards, deer, gaur (Indian bison), and several species of birds and reptiles. The sanctuary is also famous for its lush green forests, waterfalls, and trekking trails, making it a haven for nature lovers and adventure seekers. Within its boundaries lies the Dudhsagar Waterfalls, one of India's tallest and most stunning waterfalls, attracting visitors throughout the year. The Tambdi Surla Temple, a 12th-century temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, is another historical gem located inside the sanctuary. Ideal for wildlife safaris, birdwatching, and trekking, Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary offers an unforgettable experience for those looking to explore Goa’s natural beauty beyond its beaches.
